red.focus: Explain why words are read as a connected whole
red.summary: The meaning of a disputed legal phrase often depends on the words around it. Learn to explain how a definition, exception or neighboring clause changes an apparent reading.
checklist: I can identify a context clue that changes meaning
I can distinguish a general rule from its exception
I can show each step linking text to interpretation

sections.title: One Clause Can Change Another
sections.body_md: A rule says visitors may enter a building and later specifies that entry is prohibited during emergency repairs. The second clause limits the first. An interpreter who quotes only the general permission would create a false impression. This is a reasoning chain from text: identify the proposition, locate the exception, and apply both to the facts. No speculation about the author's personality is needed. The words the legal instrument uses supply the first evidence of meaning.

The words the legal instrument uses supply the first evidence of meaning.

sections.title: Define the Question First
sections.body_md: A reader asks whether a vehicle is permitted on a path. Before opening a dictionary, check whether the ordinance defines vehicle, describes the path, or distinguishes bicycles from motor cars. Each provision can affect the result. The proper interpretation must explain which text controls and why. A disagreement about meaning is not resolved by a louder assertion; it is resolved by identifying relevant legal sources and applying recognized methods.

sections.title: Text Is Not the Same as Outcome
sections.body_md: A provision may be clear but its application to an unexpected fact may be uncertain. For example, a rule drafted before electric scooters existed may not explain whether they fall under a defined category. The interpreter must distinguish uncertainty about the words from uncertainty about whether the facts satisfy them. That distinction keeps the analysis organized and helps the client understand what evidence or legal development may change the answer.

yellow.focus: Identify intent, purpose and permissible evidence
yellow.summary: Legal interpretation may involve the objective conveyed by words, the purpose of a rule and particular background materials. Learn why a court's permitted evidence depends on the instrument and jurisdiction.
checklist: I can distinguish textual meaning from an individual's private hope
I can identify when purpose or context is relevant
I can recognize limits on extrinsic material

sections.title: A Private Wish Is Not Always Meaning
sections.body_md: A contract drafter may privately intend 'delivery' to mean shipment, while the signed agreement defines it as receipt. Interpretation commonly focuses on the legally recognized meaning of the agreement rather than an uncommunicated thought. Applicable law may permit some evidence of negotiations or commercial setting while excluding other material. The student should find the governing rule before relying on a participant's later statement that they meant something different.
sections.audio_script: A contract drafter may privately intend 'delivery' to mean shipment, while the signed agreement defines it as receipt. Interpretation commonly focuses on the legally recognized meaning of the agreement rather than an uncommunicated thought. Applicable law may permit some evidence of negotiations or commercial setting while excluding other material. The student should find the governing rule before relying on a participant's later statement that they meant something different.

sections.title: Purpose Requires a Legal Anchor
sections.body_md: A statute enacted to improve road safety can guide interpretation of an ambiguous vehicle restriction, but a broad purpose does not justify ignoring clear enacted limits. The decision maker's method and permissible materials vary by jurisdiction. If a legislative report is invoked, explain whether it is a recognized aid and what precise ambiguity it addresses. Purpose is evidence for interpretation within a legal framework, not a license to replace legislative language with a preferred policy.

sections.title: Construct the Chain of Reasoning
sections.body_md: A strong interpretive paragraph identifies the disputed phrase, the related text, an applicable interpretive rule and the effect on the facts. If more than one reading remains plausible, state the competing explanations and their consequences. Avoid jumping from a desirable outcome directly to a claim about what the text must mean. This method makes disagreement precise and gives a reviewing institution reasons to accept or reject the argument.

orange.focus: Reason through treaty object, purpose and subsequent practice
orange.summary: Advanced treaty interpretation requires a structured account of the treaty text and legally relevant context. Explain when later conduct informs meaning and when supplementary materials are permitted.
checklist: I can apply Vienna Convention Article 31 coherently
I can distinguish subsequent agreement from incidental conduct
I can identify proper use of Article 32 preparatory materials

sections.title: Article 31 Works as a Whole
sections.body_md: The ordinary meaning, context, object and purpose of a treaty are analyzed in good faith under Article 31 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. A decision maker should not select whichever element most favors one state while disregarding the others. The provision also identifies further context, including certain agreements and subsequent practice establishing agreement on interpretation. That practice requires legal analysis of what states actually did and accepted, not merely a list of political speeches.
sections.audio_script: The ordinary meaning, context, object and purpose of a treaty are analyzed in good faith under Article 31 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. A decision maker should not select whichever element most favors one state while disregarding the others. The provision also identifies further context, including certain agreements and subsequent practice establishing agreement on interpretation. That practice requires legal analysis of what states actually did and accepted, not merely a list of political speeches.

sections.title: Later Practice Is Not Every Later Event
sections.body_md: A government agency may act in a way consistent with one treaty reading without thereby creating an agreement among all relevant parties. Article 31(3) sets specific standards for subsequent agreements and practice. Analyze the actors, conduct, legal relevance and evidence of agreement. The difference matters because law should not convert an isolated administrative habit into an amendment of international obligations. This is an exercise in careful inference as much as textual reading.
sections.audio_script: A government agency may act in a way consistent with one treaty reading without thereby creating an agreement among all relevant parties. Article 31(3) sets specific standards for subsequent agreements and practice. Analyze the actors, conduct, legal relevance and evidence of agreement. The difference matters because law should not convert an isolated administrative habit into an amendment of international obligations. This is an exercise in careful inference as much as textual reading.

sections.title: Supplementary Means Have Conditions
sections.body_md: Preparatory work can help confirm a treaty interpretation or address obscurity or a manifestly unreasonable result within Article 32's framework. It should not be selected opportunistically to defeat the general rule. A strong legal memorandum states the Article 31 reading first, then explains the limited role of supplementary evidence. That structure makes the claim reviewable by states, courts and persons whose rights may depend on the treaty.

black.focus: Critique claims about purpose, authorship and interpretive legitimacy
black.summary: At doctoral depth, analyze why interpreting legal meaning is not the same as reconstructing every author's private mental state. Defend interpretive methods under incomplete historical evidence and competing institutional values.
checklist: I can compare intentionalist and textual-contextual accounts
I can evaluate limits of preparatory materials
I can defend an interpretive method that makes reasons public

sections.title: The Author Is Often Many People
sections.body_md: Legislation is produced through institutions with multiple participants and compromises. A treaty is negotiated among states; a commercial agreement may be assembled by teams and standard forms. Searching for one unified private intention can be misleading. A doctoral theory must explain whose intentions count, how they are legally evidenced, and when enacted language rather than subjective hopes controls. Interpretation should produce reasons capable of being contested by people who did not participate in drafting.

A treaty is negotiated among states; a commercial agreement may be assembled by teams and standard forms. Searching for one unified private intention can be misleading. A doctoral theory must explain whose intentions count, how they are legally evidenced, and when enacted language rather than subjective hopes controls. Interpretation should produce reasons capable of being contested by people who did not participate in drafting.

sections.title: Purpose Can Multiply
sections.body_md: An enactment may seek public safety, administrative efficiency and protection of privacy at the same time. Stating a single broad purpose can obscure conflicts among enacted choices. A good interpreter grounds each purpose in the instrument and relevant legally recognized materials. Where purposes point in different directions, the argument must explain how language, structure and institutional authority resolve the tension. Sophisticated reasoning admits where a normative choice is being made rather than presenting it as inevitable.

sections.title: An Interpretive System Must Be Accountable
sections.body_md: A court that can always discover a hidden purpose supporting its favored outcome risks undermining public notice and democratic authority. A court that refuses to adapt general language to unforeseen facts may also fail the purpose law was designed to serve. The doctoral task is to specify transparent constraints, methods of review and standards for legitimate development. Interpretive power should be exercised with reasons people can examine, especially when it controls freedom, property or protection from violence.
